newsitem.title: UK: Exportable 98/99 coffee crop may top 80 mln - EIU.
newsitem.headline: Exportable 98/99 coffee crop may top 80 mln - EIU.

text.p: The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) said world's 1997/98 exportable coffee production could top 80 million 60-kg bags for the first time in history, spearheaded by a cyclical upturn in Brazil.
For comparison, the exportable crop is estimated at 78.4 million bags in 1997/98 and 74.1 million in 1996/97, it said.
The London-based think tank said new plantings of recent years should also boost 1998/99 Brazil output.
Government efforts to increase production have already been signalled in other countries including Mexico, it said in its third quarter commodity forecast report.
Better sales returns in 1997 are also encouraging spending on farm inputs.
The EIU said recent worries about the possible return of the El Nino weather pattern seemed premature.
"Although this could mean drier than usual weather in Indonesia in 1998, which would reduce supplies, it could also lessen the risk of frosts in Brazil," the group said.
